comments.text:
I use to deliver for a terrible furniture company in Florida called City Furniture.
So much of this was far to common.
Sales people would do what ever they had to do and say what ever they had to say to make the sell. Even promising customers that i would do things outside of my duties.
Something being in stock when you buy something only means it is in the building at the time of purchase. What inventory wont show is that it is about to get pulled that night for delivery the next day and who knows when another will get in stock.
Then the added fun, we the delivery drivers, we're also paid by comission. Wether all we had to do was drop it off or actually assemble the items, the pay was the same too. So each morning i would get my assigned route and be able to see what the most i coule profit for that day and see my drive time and work load. But then a damaged item here, backorder there, or even the delivery being scheduled for the wrong day and all i could do is watch my pay for the day shrink more and more. And since it is commission they push for us to "protect our money" which basically translates to hide the problems and do everything we can to keep the product in the house. Plus, the cheaper the product, the more work is involved in assembling the product. So i could have some deliveries where I made a whole $5 to deliver someting that took me half an hour to assemble as well as driving to the customer, putting it where they want, and deal with finalizing the delivery.

Now with that, They were also partnered with Ashley. So i am well aware with both their quality and more importantly because of what he kept saying, their cost.
Ashley is one of the most cheapest furniture brands on the market. It is all particle board with wall paper covering it to make it look half decent. I'd see whole bedroom sets not including a mattress cost like $600. So him constantly saying "I spent a lot of money" is basically the equivilant as to someone that bought a car saying they spent a lot of money, but that car was a Nissan Versa. Not defending the furniture company because I feel like they can be scummier than car salesman, but him constantly saying that line made me feel like he was being a "Darren".
